documents_checked.document_title: Acceptable Use of Information Systems Policy
documents_checked.text:
This policy and its associated operational documents apply to all Authorised Users of the
University’s Information and Communication Technology (ICT) environment.
Included in scope are all University Information Systems, regardless of their location, and any
devices connected to the University’s networks, including where members of the University
Community bring their own devices for use whilst at the University.
DEFINITIONS:

documents_checked.document_title: Acceptable Use of Information Systems Policy
documents_checked.text:
Authorised Users provided with accounts enabling access to University Information Systems
accept accounts on the understanding they are for the exclusive use of the Authorised User
and must not be shared or used by anyone other than the Authorised User.
Passwords, accounts and documented processes required for the access of University
information must be protected and secured in accordance with the conditions under which
access has been provided.
Authorised Users must not deliberately avoid or attempt to avoid authentication or conceal or
attempt to conceal their identity whilst using University information Systems.

documents_checked.text:
provide an annual consolidated report on academic integrity within the University, to each Unit
Review Committee and to the Academic Board; and
maintain and secure confidential records of academic integrity allegations, breaches,
investigations and outcomes, in accordance with the University’s Privacy Policy, Records
Management Policy and any other applicable law.
Each School will respond to the Deputy Vice-Chancellor (Students and Education)’s annual
report, for submission to Academic Board, addressing the following in relation to their School
or Teaching Area:
data and trends relating to concerns, allegations and findings of Academic Breach and
Academic Misconduct for Students;
the manner in which allegations were dealt with;
the steps taken to promote academic integrity and to minimise Academic Breach and
Academic Misconduct; and
action plans to continuously improve academic integrity.

case_summary.critical_risk_criterion: Verified authority for standing account actions, protected student identity and meaningful assessment oversight.
case_summary.critical_gap_explanation: N093 strictly prohibits sharing accounts or concealing identity on University systems, and N090 and N154 enforce student authorship and Student Identity Verification, preventing standing autonomous agent submissions.
case_summary.case_note: ECU prohibits delegating standing account authority to an autonomous AI agent under N093, which restricts University accounts to exclusive personal use and forbids concealing user identity. Submitting coursework without human review also breaches N090 own-work requirements and N154 Student Identity Verification rules. Protocol v1.1 was adopted after preliminary review; referenced Statute 22 and Academic Misconduct Rules sit outside the bundle.

supporting_passages.text:
This policy applies to:
Complaints made by prospective, current and former Students or members of the public about
the University or University-related conduct, whether occurring in Australia or overseas; and
all persons involved in making, responding to, managing or resolving those Complaints.
Where legislation or another University or external framework provides a specific process for
dealing with all or part of a matter, the University may refer or manage that matter under the
applicable process. This includes matters concerning academic review or appeal, public
interest disclosures, misconduct, staff performance, privacy, employment or workplace
grievances, the ECU Student Guild, and third-party organisations.
This does not prevent the University from considering a distinct Complaint about its
administration of, or response to, the matter.
Where a matter engages more than one framework, the University will determine whether the
relevant issues are to be managed separately, sequentially, concurrently or in a coordinated
manner and will inform the Complainant of the applicable pathway.
